items.title: Bob Rosengarden interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 6, 1996
items.q: And I hired two bass players, Milt Hinton and George Duvivier.

ctx.x: Did you give them the song titles?

Oh well I found a gimmick that worked for me. Since Cavett did not have a musical ear, does not have a musical ear, he used to say, I used to kind of begrudge it but I really, it was a compliment. He said, “I don’t know anything too much about music, but everybody tells me this band is wonderful.” Which is a typical Cavett remark, you know? And we’d all go ahhhh. But it’s the best band in town. And I picked anybody I wanted. The job paid a lot of money, it was staff orchestra at ABC. That’s when the three…
What was a typical day, how did it run for that show? © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -6-

items.title: Milt Hinton interviewed by Joe Williams, Majesty of the Seas, May 31, 1995
items.q: you were doing the, with Bobby Rosengarden, you were doing the television show.

ctx.x: I remember Bob Cranshaw looking over my shoulder, I’ve got pictures of him looking over my shoulder observing what is required of him. Now he’s in the recording studio.
That’s true. But you know the thing about that that was so beautiful, you were doing the, with Bobby Rosengarden, you were doing the television show. What’s the boy’s name?
